explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-based evaluation metrics (GPTScore and G-Eval variants) against human evaluation results using correlation analysis on the same set of summaries, reporting quantitative correlation metrics

prompts.notes: Exact prompts provided in Appendix E.2 including scoring scales and evaluation instructions for both GPTScore (text-filling) and G-Eval (5-point rating) methods

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: high agreement compared to prior collections (RealSumm: 0.66, SummEval: 0.49)

guidelines.notes: Detailed ACU annotation protocol described in §3 including ACU writing and matching procedures with examples provided in Table 13 and Appendix D.1

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted across entire RoSE benchmark consisting of 22,000 summary-level annotations over three datasets (CNNDM, XSum, SamSum)

quantitative_scores.notes: System-level correlation with GPT-3.5 sampling variant

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-based evaluation metrics (GPTScore and G-Eval variants) cannot outperform traditional metrics like ROUGE on the RoSE benchmark, showing weak to moderate correlations with human ACU annotations across datasets.

criteria_mapping.notes: Human evaluation uses ACU protocol for salience measurement across all protocols, while LLM metrics are specifically validated against ACU-based human annotations for salience/coverage criteria
